summary: The BMW 3 Series (E46) is the fourth 3 Series generation. BMW built these compact executive cars from 1997 to 2006. It succeeded the E36 3 Series. It came as a sedan, coupé, convertible, station wagon and hatchback. The hatchback was sold as the 3 Series Compact. Development began in 1993. Chris Bangle led design from late 1993. Erik Goplen of DesignworksUSA designed the approved exterior. BMW claimed the body was 70% more rigid than the E36's. It kept rear-wheel drive and 50/50 weight distribution. All-wheel drive returned on some models. It was the first 3 Series offered with Valvetronic. It added satellite navigation, rain-sensing wipers and LED tail-lights. It was built in Germany and South Africa. Sales peaked in 2002 at 561,249 cars. The M3 arrived in 2000 with the S54 straight-six. A lighter M3 CSL followed. The E90 began replacing it from late 2004. Coupés and convertibles continued until 2006. Andy Priaulx won 2004 and 2005 touring car titles in a 320i.
